consistency_note: No POV exists, so there is no journey to be consistent with. The 68 s of landscape tram exterior splits into one hazy daytime clip (6112102, trams small in background) and two sped-up night clips from one shooter in Causeway Bay (group a). Landmark footage is mostly night (skyline 46 s, Tsuen Wan light-trail timelapses, minibus terminus tilt-shift, drone hyperlapse) plus one teal-graded hazy daytime harbour shot. A coherent 'Hong Kong at night' montage of about 130 s (group a trams + night landmarks) is possible, but four of those clips are timelapse/long-exposure stylised and would not cut against real-time footage. Daytime material is two unrelated clips (45 s) with different grades.
sourcing_note: Hard. pexels.com is blocked so discovery was only via web search restricted to pexels.com, which mostly returns photo pages and the same 4-5 video pages for every Hong Kong tram/MTR query. Useful terms: 'Hong Kong tram', 'Victoria Harbour Hong Kong skyline', 'Hong Kong ... timelapse night traffic'. 'MTR', 'Peak Tram', 'Kowloon neon', 'view from train window Hong Kong' returned zero matching videos (only photos or generic non-HK train clips). Not found at all: any MTR train (exterior or POV), any Peak Tram video, any view from inside a tram/train in Hong Kong. Structural limit: fetch_pexels.sh resolved nothing with an id above about 21 million, so every recent upload (10 HK candidates, including both clips whose titles explicitly say Hong Kong tram) could not be downloaded or viewed. Three counted clips were found by probing ids adjacent to confirmed ones. The repo sheet.sh fails on this machine's ffmpeg (pad filter error, writes no image); sheets were made with an equivalent script kept outside the repo (4 frames per clip at 10/35/60/85%), saved as work/audit/hong_kong/sheet_1..4.jpg.
